The format varies by import type:\n85\t///\n86\t/// - **For `use` statements**: Full module path being imported (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`,\n87\t///   `\"crate::module::Item\"`, `\"super::ParentModule\"`)\n88\t/// - **For `extern crate`**: The crate name (e.g., `\"serde\"`, `\"tokio\"`)\n89\t/// - **For `mod`**: The module name (e.g., `\"foo\"`, `\"bar\"`)\n90\t///\n91\t/// **Constraints:**\n92\t/// - Non-empty string (cannot be `\"\"`)\n93\t/// - Contains only valid Rust identifier characters and path separators (`::`)\n94\t/// - Case-sensitive (matches Rust's rules)\n95\t///\n96\t/// **Usage in practice:**\n97\t/// ```rust\n98\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n99\t///\n100\t/// // Standard library import\n101\t/// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n102\t///\n103\t/// // Crate-relative import\n104\t/// let crate_import = Import::new(\"crate::module::Item\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n105\t///\n106\t/// // External crate\n107\t/// let extern_import = Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1);\n108\t/// ```\n109\t///\n110\t/// ## `import_type: ImportType`\n111\t///\n112\t/// The type classification of the import statement. This field distinguishes between the three\n113\t/// fundamental kinds of import statements in Rust:\n114\t///\n115\t/// - **[`ImportType::Use`]**: Standard `use` statements (most common)\n116\t/// - **[`ImportType::ExternCrate`]**: External crate declarations\n117\t/// - **[`ImportType::Mod`]**: Module declarations\n118\t///\n119\t/// **Valid values:** Only the three variants defined in [`ImportType`]\n120\t///\n121\t/// **Usage in practice:**\n122\t/// ```rust\n123\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n124\t///\n125\t/// // Categorize imports by type\n126\t/// fn is_standard_library(import: &Import) -> bool {\n127\t///     match import.import_type {\n128\t///         ImportType::Use => import.path.starts_with(\"std::\") || import.path.starts_with(\"core::\"),\n129\t///         _ => false,\n130\t///     }\n131\t/// }\n132\t///\n133\t/// let std_import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n134\t/// assert!(is_standard_library(&std_import));\n135\t/// ```\n136\t///\n137\t/// ## `line_number: usize`\n138\t///\n139\t/// The 1-indexed line number where the import statement appears in the source file.\n140\t///\n141\t/// **Constraints:**\n142\t/// - Must be ≥ 1 (1-indexed, not 0-indexed)\n143\t/// - Should be ≤ total lines in the source file\n144\t/// - Used for source location and error reporting\n145\t///\n146\t/// **Usage in practice:**\n147\t/// ```rust\n148\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n149\t///\n150\t/// // Track import location for error reporting\n151\t/// let import = Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 42);\n152\t///\n153\t/// println!(\"Import found at line {}\", import.line_number);\n154\t/// // Output: Import found at line 42\n155\t///\n156\t/// // Compare import locations\n157\t/// let import1 = Import::new(\"foo\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n158\t/// let import2 = Import::new(\"bar\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 20);\n159\t///\n160\t/// assert!(import1.line_number < import2.line_number);\n161\t/// ```\n162\t///\n163\t/// # Examples\n164\t///\n165\t/// ## Creating different import types\n166\t///\n167\t/// ```rust\n168\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n169\t///\n170\t/// // Create a standard library use import\n171\t/// let std_import = Import::new(\n172\t///     \"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(),\n173\t///     ImportType::Use,\n174\t///     15\n175\t/// );\n176\t///\n177\t/// // Create an external crate import\n178\t/// let extern_import = Import::new(\n179\t///     \"serde\".to_string(),\n180\t///     ImportType::ExternCrate,\n181\t///     3\n182\t/// );\n183\t///\n184\t/// // Create a module declaration\n185\t/// let mod_import = Import::new(\n186\t///     \"my_module\".to_string(),\n187\t///     ImportType::Mod,\n188\t///     8\n189\t/// );\n190\t///\n191\t/// assert_eq!(std_import.import_type, ImportType::Use);\n192\t/// assert_eq!(extern_import.import_type, ImportType::ExternCrate);\n193\t/// assert_eq!(mod_import.import_type, ImportType::Mod);\n194\t/// ```\n195\t///\n196\t/// ## Working with imports programmatically\n197\t///\n198\t/// ```rust\n199\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n200\t///\n201\t/// let imports = vec![\n202\t///     Import::new(\"std::collections::HashMap\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5),\n203\t///     Import::new(\"serde\".to_string(), ImportType::ExternCrate, 1),\n204\t///     Import::new(\"crate::module::Item\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10),\n205\t/// ];\n206\t///\n207\t/// // Count imports by type\n208\t/// let use_count = imports.iter()\n209\t///     .filter(|i| i.import_type == ImportType::Use)\n210\t///     .count();\n211\t///\n212\t/// assert_eq!(use_count, 2);\n213\t///\n214\t/// // Find standard library imports\n215\t/// let std_libs: Vec<_> = imports.iter()\n216\t///     .filter(|i| i.path.starts_with(\"std::\"))\n217\t///     .collect();\n218\t///\n219\t/// assert_eq!(std_libs.len(), 1);\n220\t/// ```\n221\t///\n222\t/// ## Import equality and comparison\n223\t///\n224\t/// ```rust\n225\t/// use agentscribe::parser::{Import, ImportType};\n226\t///\n227\t/// let import1 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n228\t/// let import2 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 5);\n229\t/// let import3 = Import::new(\"std::fs\".to_string(), ImportType::Use, 10);\n230\t///\n231\t/// // Same path, type, and line number are equal\n232\t/// assert_eq!(import1, import2);\n233\t///\n234\t/// // Different line numbers are not equal\n235\t/// assert_ne!(import1, import3);\n236\t/// ```\n237\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize)]\n238\tpub struct Import {\n239\t    /// The import path (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`, `\"crate::module::Item\"`)\n240\t    ///\n241\t    /// Contains the full module path being imported. The format varies by import type:\n242\t    ///\n243\t    /// - **For `use` statements**: Full module path (e.g., `\"std::collections::HashMap\"`,\n244\t    ///   `\"crate::module::Item\"`, `\"super::ParentModule\"`)\n245\t    /// - **For `extern crate`**: The crate name (e.g., `\"serde\"`, `\"tokio\"`)\n246\t    /// - **For `mod`**: The module name (e.g., `\"foo\"`, `\"bar\"`)\n247\t    ///\n248\t    /// # Valid Values\n249\t    ///\n250\t    /// -    /// Represents the position in the source file where this import statement is located.\n334\t    /// Line numbers start at 1 (not 0) to match standard text editor and compiler line JSON using dot notation\n455\tpub fn extract_field(value: &Value, path: &str) -> Option<Value> {\n456\t    if path.is_empty() {\n457\t        return None;\n458\t    }\n459\t\n460\t    let mut current = value;\n461\t    for part in path.split('.') {\n462\t        // Handle array indexing like parts[0]\n463\t        if let Some(bracket_pos) = part.find('[') {\n464\t            let key = current.get(key)?.get(index)?;\n469\t        } else {\n470\t            current = current.get(part)?;\n471\t        }\n472\t    }\n473\t    Some(current.clone())\n474\t}\n475\t\n476\t/// Extract a extract_string(value, path)\n491\t        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n492\t\n493\t    // Try ISO 8601 first\n494\t    if let Ok(dt) = payload only\n560\t        extract_field(payload, path)\n561\t    }\n562\t}\n563\t\n564\t/// Extract a string field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n565\t///\n566\t/// Wrapper          })\n596\t                .collect();\n597\t            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n598\t                None\n599\t            } else {\n600\t                Some(text_parts.join(\" '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n619\t\n620\t    // Try ISO 8601 first\n621\t    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n622\t        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n623\t    }\n624\t\n625\t    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n626\t    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n627\t        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n628\t            // Milliseconds\n629\t            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n630\t        } else {\n631\t            // Seconds\n632\t            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n633\t        };\n634\t        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n635\t    }\n636\t\n637\t    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n638\t    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n639\t        return Ok(dt);\n640\t    }\n641\t\n642\t    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n643\t        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n644\t        ts_str\n645\t    )))\n646\t}\n647\t\n648\t/// Base trait for all format parsers\n649\tpub trait FormatParser {\n650\t    /// Parse events from the source\n651\t    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n652\t\n653\t    /// Parse events from the source, starting from a given byte offset for incremental parsing.\n654\t    ///\n655\t    /// For formats that support incremental parsing (JSONL, append-only logs), this allows\n656\t    /// the parser to skip already-processed content and only parse new data.\n657\t    ///\n658\t    /// # Arguments\n659\t    ///\n660\t    /// * `source_path` - Path to the source file\n661\t    /// * `plugin` - Plugin configuration for this source\n662\t    /// * `start_offset` - Byte offset to start reading from (0 for full parse)\n663\t    ///\n664\t    /// # Returns\n665\t    ///\n666\t    /// - `Ok(events)` - Vector of parsed events\n667\t    /// - `Err(_)` - Parse error (check `is_skippable()` for non-fatal errors)\n668\t    fn parse_incremental(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin, start_offset: u64) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n669\t        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n670\t        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n671\t        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n672\t    }\n673\t\n674\t    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n675\t    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n676\t}\n677\t\n678\t/// Information about a detected session\n679\t#[derive(Debug, Option<Value>,\n686\t    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n687\t    /// is a child of another session)\n688\t    pub parent_session_id:      // Unicode and special characters\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^_field\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^$field\"));\n        assert!(has_caret_prefix(\"^field-name\"));\n ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Extract a field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// **Envelope-first with payload fallback for caret-prefixed paths:**\n/// - If path starts with `^`, try envelope first (remove `^` prefix)\n/// - If envelope is None OR field not found in envelope, fallback to payload\n/// - Otherwise, extract from payload only\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `^field`:**\n/// 1. Try `envelope.field` (if envelope exists)\n/// 2. Fallback to `payload.field` (if envelope missing or field not found)\n/// 3. Return None (if both fail)\n///\n/// **Resolution order for `field` (no caret):**\n/// - Extract from `payload.field` only\n///\n/// Supports dot notation for nested fields (e.g., `^outer.ts` or `user.role`)\n/// and array indexing (e.g., `items[0].name`).\npub fn extract_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<Value> {\n    if has_caret_prefix(path) {\n        // Strip the caret prefix\n        if let Some(envelope_path) = path.strip_prefix('^') {\n            // Try envelope first\n            if let Some(env) = envelope {\n                if let Some(value) = extract_field(env, envelope_path) {\n                    return Some(value); // Found in envelope\n                }\n            }\n            // Fallback to payload (using path without ^)\n            extract_field(payload, envelope_path)\n        } else {\n            // Should not happen due to starts_with check, but handle defensively\n            None\n        }\n    } else {\n        // No caret prefix - extract from payload only\n        extract_field(payload, path)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Extract a string field from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_with_envelope` that converts the raw `Value` to a string,\n/// following the same coercion rules as `extract_string` (String, Number, Bool, Null).\npub fn extract_string_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Option<String> {\n    let value = extract_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)?;\n    match value {\n        Value::String(s) => Some(s),\n        Value::Number(n) => Some(n.to_string()),\n        Value::Bool(b) => Some(b.to_string()),\n        Value::Null => Some(String::new()),\n        Value::Array(arr) => {\n            // Handle content arrays (e.g., Claude Code format with text blocks and tool calls)\n            // Extract text from all text blocks in the array\n            let text_parts: Vec<String> = arr\n                .iter()\n                .filter_map(|item| {\n                    if let Some(obj) = item.as_object() {\n                        // Check for text blocks: {\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"...\"}\n                        if obj.get(\"type\").and_then(|t| t.as_str()) == Some(\"text\") {\n                            return obj\n                                .get(\"text\")\n                                .and_then(|t| t.as_str())\n                                .map(|s| s.to_string());\n                        }\n                    }\n                    None\n                })\n                .collect();\n            if text_parts.is_empty() {\n                None\n            } else {\n                Some(text_parts.join(\" \"))\n            }\n        }\n        _ => None,\n    }\n}\n\n/// Parse a timestamp from either envelope or payload based on path prefix\n///\n/// Wrapper around `extract_string_with_envelope` that parses the extracted string\n/// as a timestamp. Supports ISO 8601, Unix epoch (seconds/milliseconds), and\n/// UTC-naive formats.\npub fn parse_timestamp_with_envelope(\n    path: &str,\n    payload: &Value,\n    envelope: Option<&Value>,\n) -> Result<DateTime<Utc>> {\n    let ts_str = extract_string_with_envelope(path, payload, envelope)\n        .ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\"Field '{}' not found\", path)))?;\n\n    // Try ISO 8601 first\n    if let Ok(dt) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&ts_str) {\n        return Ok(dt.with_timezone(&Utc));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing as Unix epoch (seconds)\n    if let Ok(seconds) = ts_str.parse::<i64>() {\n        let ts = if seconds > 1_000_000_000_000 {\n            // Milliseconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp_millis(seconds)\n        } else {\n            // Seconds\n            DateTime::from_timestamp(seconds, 0)\n        };\n        return ts.ok_or_else(|| AgentScribeError::Timestamp(\"Invalid timestamp\".to_string()));\n    }\n\n    // Try parsing without timezone (assume UTC)\n    if let Ok(dt) = ts_str.parse::<DateTime<Utc>>() {\n        return Ok(dt);\n    }\n\n    Err(AgentScribeError::Timestamp(format!(\n        \"Cannot parse timestamp: {}\",\n        ts_str\n    )))\n}\n\n/// Base trait for all format parsers\npub trait FormatParser {\n    /// Parse events from the source\n    fn parse(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<Event>>;\n\n    /// Parse events from the source, starting from a given byte offset for incremental parsing.\n    ///\n    /// For formats that support incremental parsing (JSONL, append-only logs), this allows\n    /// the parser to skip already-processed content and only parse new data.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    ///\n    /// * `source_path` - Path to the source file\n    /// * `plugin` - Plugin configuration for this source\n    /// * `start_offset` - Byte offset to start reading from (0 for full parse)\n    ///\n    /// # Returns\n    ///\n    /// - `Ok(events)` - Vector of parsed events\n    /// - `Err(_)` - Parse error (check `is_skippable()` for non-fatal errors)\n    fn parse_incremental(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin, start_offset: u64) -> Result<Vec<Event>> {\n        // Default implementation falls back to full parse\n        let _ = start_offset; // Suppress unused warning\n        self.parse(source_path, plugin)\n    }\n\n    /// Detect session boundaries in the source\n    fn detect_sessions(&self, source_path: &Path, plugin: &Plugin) -> Result<Vec<SessionInfo>>;\n}\n\n/// Information about a detected session\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\n#[allow(dead_code)]\npub struct SessionInfo {\n    pub session_id: String,\n    pub start_offset: u64,\n    pub end_offset: u64,\n    pub metadata: Option<Value>,\n    /// Parent session ID (populated for subagent sessions where this session\n    /// is a child of another session)\n    pub parent_session_id: Option<String>,\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n    use serde_json::json;\n\n    // Tests for Import and ImportType types\n\n    #[test]\n    fn test_import_type_creation() {\n
